title: Codes: capitals and empty tokens
where: Mitigation H6668:H7397 (8 pollutant blocks, 90 cells) and policy H12984:H13713; 67 codes with an empty scenario token (H2320, H3225:H3233, H3315:H3323, H3474:H3482, H3643:H3644, H7589:H7590, H7620, G17215 and policy copies)
why: (1) Capitals: the code formulas of the "All" rows of the local-pollutant blocks join the label in column D ("All") into the code, so the code reads em.pm2.All.pow.1 against the lower-case protocol (180 codes). (2) Empty tokens: 67 codes end with "." because their scenario number points to a blank cell (C2175, C2184, C2033, C2186, C2174, C2165, C$1678; policy C8491, C8500, C8349, C8502, C8490, C8481, C$1678) instead of C2173 (policy C8489). A lookup of the protocol code fails: results row 16236 (current carbon tax on industrial electricity, ctx.ind.ecy.t.1) finds nothing and IFNA returns 0. Adding the number alone would make some codes equal to another row's: rows 3315-3323 (levelised transmission costs) would take fix.pow.<type>.t.1 of rows 3247-3255 (levelised fixed costs), rows 3474-3482 (generation costs before storage and carbon tax) gnc of rows 3486-3494, row 7589 (fugitive N2O) the CH4 code of row 7588 (its gas token is ch4), row 7590 (fugitive total) the total of row 7586. Those rows get their own variable token; rows 3225-3233 are copies of rows 3282-3290 (=L3282) and lose their code.
